title: Giants sign WR Braxton Berrios; Odell Beckham Jr. remains a free agent
content:
A New York Giants-Odell Beckham Jr. reunion isn’t in the cards — at least not right now. Despite hosting the veteran wide receiver and longtime fan-favorite for a second workout this offseason, the Giants opted to sign free agent receiver/returner Braxton Berrios to a one-year deal, a league source confirmed to The Athletic.

Berrios worked out alongside Beckham, as well as veterans Juju Smith-Schuster and Anthony Miller on Monday. Berrios, 30 joins the team a few days after primary returner Gunner Olszewski tore his Achilles during OTAs. Of the group of veteran receivers who worked out for the team on Monday, Berrios’ skill set is the closest match to Olszewski’s. Berrios has plenty of similarities to Olszewski, as they both began their careers in New England (Berrios was a 2018 sixth-round pick; Olszewski was an undrafted rookie in 2019).

The 5-foot-9, 185-pound Berrios found success as a returner after getting cut by the Patriots after one season and landing with the Jets in 2019. Berrios was named a first-team All-Pro in 2021 after averaging 13.4 yards per punt return and 30.4 yards per kickoff return, highlighted by a 102-yard kick return touchdown. The 6-foot, 190-pound Olszewski was a first-team All-Pro for the Patriots in 2020 after averaging an NFL-high 17.3 yards per punt return and 23.2 yards per kickoff return.

Berrios, who has primarily lined up in the slot, has more career production as a receiver than Olszewski. Berrios set career-highs with 46 catches for 431 yards for the Jets in 2021. The 30-year-old’s production has tailed off in recent seasons. Berrios suffered a torn ACL in Week 7 of the 2024 season while a member of the Dolphins. He appeared in just four games last season for the Texans as he dealt with a hamstring injury early in the season and then was buried on the depth chart.

Berrios enters a punt return competition that includes Calvin Austin III and Xavier Gipson.

As for Beckham, the 33-year-old and 2014 Giants first-round pick had previously worked out for the team and underwent a physical in the week leading up to the NFL Draft. In his post-draft press conference, coach John Harbaugh said Beckham “looked good,” and said the two sides would continue to remain in touch.

“It’s got to be right for both parties,” said Harbaugh, who coached Beckham in Baltimore in 2023, during rookie minicamp. “Odell wants to be the kind of player that can make a difference. I’m pretty sure that he can make a team in the National Football League right now, but can he make a difference? It’s something he wants to do. Is his body going to hold up in the way he wants it to, and all those things are questions that need to get answered for anybody at that age.

“You know Odell. He’s confident, man. He’s confident. He’s working hard. He believes in himself. I think we’ll just play it out over the next month and into training camp and see where we’re at.”

Before his workout with the team on Monday, Beckham spent some quality time over the weekend with the Giants at Brian Burns’ Celebrity Charity Softball Game. While Beckham did not speak with members of the media, Burns said he would be thrilled if the veteran receiver returned to New York.

“I think he would be a great teammate,” Burns said. “I grew up a little bit watching him. He’s definitely a dog. Over the years, just being around each other, being in the same circles, we crossed paths a couple times and had some conversations, so I think it’d be great to have him in the locker room.”

Perhaps there can still be reunion with Beckham somewhere down the road, but for now, the Giants are moving forward with Berrios.
